hints: A de Bruijn sequence must contain every length-n bit string exactly once as a cyclic window.
Make each length-(n-1) bit string a graph vertex; each length-n string is an edge from its prefix to suffix.
Find an Euler cycle through all edges and read edge labels to form the sequence.
analogy: Turn each n-bit window into a directed edge; traversing each edge once lines up all windows in one cyclic string.
example: For n=2, the cyclic sequence 0011 has windows 00,01,11,10, all four bit strings.
algorithm: Build the binary de Bruijn graph and find an Eulerian circuit with Hierholzer. Output the starting n-1 bits followed by each traversed edge's final bit.
correctness: Each graph edge represents one distinct n-bit string; an Euler tour uses each edge once, and consecutive edge endpoints overlap in n-1 bits, yielding the required windows.
